name: SYD
description: SYD returns the depreciation of an asset for a given period using the sum-of-years-digits method, which accelerates depreciation faster than straight-line but slower than double-declining.
tldr: Calculates sum-of-years-digits depreciation for a specified period.

parameters.name: salvage
parameters.description: Value at the end of the depreciation life.

parameters.name: life
parameters.description: Number of periods over which the asset is depreciated.

parameters.name: per
parameters.description: The period for which to calculate depreciation.

basicExample.explanation: A $10,000 asset with 5-year life depreciates $2,666.67 in the first year using sum-of-years-digits.

advancedExamples.title: Later year depreciation
advancedExamples.explanation: Depreciation is highest in early years and lowest in later years.

howItWorks: SYD multiplies the depreciable cost (cost - salvage) by a fraction. The numerator is the remaining life, and the denominator is the sum of the years digits (e.g., 1+2+3+4+5 = 15).

howToSteps.name: Calculate
howToSteps.text: Press Enter to get the result.

limitations: Produces higher depreciation in early years.

commonErrors.cause: Per is less than 1 or greater than life.
commonErrors.fix: Ensure per is between 1 and life.

commonErrors.cause: Per argument refers to a different period than expected.
commonErrors.fix: Confirm that per matches the period you want.

googleSheetsEquivalent.description: SYD works identically in Google Sheets.
googleSheetsEquivalent.notes: Same syntax and behavior as Excel.

faq.question: What is the difference between SYD and DDB?
faq.answer: SYD uses a declining fraction based on remaining life. DDB uses a fixed rate multiplied by remaining book value.

faq.question: Is SYD still used for taxes?
faq.answer: It is less common now; many tax systems use MACRS or straight-line.
